analysis.title: Multi-Asset Strategy Daily
key_insights: USTs are caught between resilient US data and fragile risk sentiment. Stronger October retail sales pushed 2Y UST yields briefly to 4.85%, and Musalem's warning that "several" further hikes may be needed added to the bear-flattening. The renewed equity sell-off then pulled 2Y yields back below 4.80% and 10Y below 5.10%.
The flight-to-quality bid extended in Asian hours as the post-Nvidia bounce in S&P futures faded. Another leg lower in equities should keep a bid under duration. DXY held Tuesday's gains near 103.68.

Brent slipped back below $92 despite further US-Iran escalation. Bahrain said it intercepted fresh Iranian attacks overnight after a US strike on an Iranian missile site at Qeshm, and Hormuz disruption continues. Large API builds in crude and gasoline keep the bearish supply story in control for now.

FOMC minutes are the main macro event. December is fully priced and about 80bp of tightening is priced through Sep-27, so Mizuho would need clearly hawkish minutes to materially extend the front-end sell-off.

EGBs should keep a modest flight-to-quality bid. German 10Y yields ended about 0.5bp lower after the early rally was unwound by strong US data, Musalem's comments and the oil rebound. Lagarde, the ECB Financial Stability Review and final euro-area CPI are the local focus.

Le Pen's proposal pairing a lower retirement age with a funded private savings scheme was well received and took the 10Y OAT-Bund spread from about 157bp to 152.5bp or below. Mizuho cautions against extrapolating because longer-term fiscal implications point the other way.
EUR/USD is back to recent lows below 1.0980, consistent with the firmer dollar and the wide US-EUR rate differential.

UK October headline CPI rose to 3.6% YoY, driven largely by energy, while core was unchanged at 2.8%. Services CPI missed slightly at 3.7% against expectations of an acceleration. RPI was a modest upside surprise at 4.2%.

With no clear wage acceleration and soft services CPI, Mizuho says the data can buy the BoE time to hike more gradually than the SONIA curve prices, especially if oil stays weak. Mizuho expects the strip to find a bid. GBP/USD is near 1.3175, around recent lows.
In Asia, equities improved after Nvidia's results but the move lost steam through the session. JGBs twist-steepened after a soft 20Y auction. USD/JPY traded in a tight range near 159.35.
earnings_insights: Nvidia results gave Asian equities and S&P futures an initial bounce that faded. The report gives no EPS or revenue figures.
